newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault denies paying Belgian party.
newsitem.headline: Dassault denies paying Belgian party.

text.p: French aircraft maker Dassault Aviation on Tuesday denied a Belgian newspaper report it paid 1.2 million francs to the Belgian Flemish Christian Democratic Party (CVP) in 1987.
"I can only once again deny it. We are not making any other comment," a Dassault spokesman said.

The CVP, now led by Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, however confirmed a report in the De Morgen newspaper that it received the money, with a party spokesman saying gifts were legal until 1989, under a law on party financing.
This is the first time Dassault has been linked to the CVP party.
Dassault has previously denied reports it allegedly paid 10 million francs in bribes for the Carapace contract to modernise electronics for Belgian air force F16 and Mirages combat planes.
The Belgian justice authorities last May issued an international arrest warrant for Dassault chairman Serge Dassault, for questioning in connection with the bribery allegations.

The latest accusation follows a report in the De Morgen daily which said the independent Oversight Committee had given the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, a report saying Dassault made the payment in December 1987, when Wilfred Martens headed the then Democrat-Liberation coalition.
